The '''Kwa''' were an ancient species native to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] that built the [[Infinity Gate]]s and [[Star Temple]]s during the [[Pre-Republic era]].<ref name="ff" /> The Infinity Gates were permanent structures capable of enabling instantaneous travel between interstellar locations and were housed within the Star Temples.<ref name="TEA" />

==Biology and appearance==
Kwa were bipedal, three-[[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, cobalt-blue-skinned [[Species/Legends#Reptilian sentient species|saurians]] with [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] abilities. They also had the ability to run at incredible speeds.<ref name="ff" />

==History==
===Rise of the Kwa===
{{Quote|Attuned to the Power of the Cosmos, my people traveled the galaxy via Infinity Gates&mdash;portals that transported us instantly between great distances. We observed many worlds and brought civilization to their people.|[[A'nang]]|<ref name="DOTJ 8">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 3]]</ref>}}
The Kwa originated on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]],<ref name="TEA" /> although there was some evidence for their [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] origin. They invented the [[Infinity Gate]]s which enabled instantaneous travel between various interstellar locations.<ref name="ff" /> However, they could also operate as [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] known as the [[Infinity Wave]] since they were modeled on a [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] concept. These were housed within vast pyramidal structures known as the [[Star Temple]]s.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Iktotch_Kwa.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Kwa showing the power of the Force to primitive Iktotchi.]]
This technology enabled them to carve up a regional empire known as the [[Kwa holdings]] that became a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] power hundreds of thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. By [[100,000 BBY]], they shared the galaxy with a number of other races, including the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]], [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]], [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]], [[Columi/Legends|Columi]], [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]], [[Taung/Legends|Taung]], and [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. Around that [[Time/Legends|time]], however, the possession of such a powerful weapon as the Infinity Wave led them to [[Gree-Kwa conflict|border disputes]] with the [[Gree Enclave/Legends|Gree Empire]].<ref name="TEA" /> During these times the Kwa, along with both the Gree and Killiks, became servants of the Celestials. This era saw them aid in building astonishing technological projects.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===Decline===
{{Quote|The Rakata are a pestilence upon the galaxy that, to our shame, we, the Kwa, unleashed.|A'nang|<ref name="DOTJ 9">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Battle_of_Lehon.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Conflict between the Kwa and the burgeoning Infinite Empire.]]
Through their Infinity Gates, the Kwa arrived on the planet [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] where they encountered the primitive [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]]. During this encounter, they sensed that the native species were strong Force-sensitives and they uplifted them as the Kwa had done to many other worlds. This saw the Rakata gaining knowledge of the Force and they were also given advanced technology. In time, the Kwa discovered that they had made a grievous mistake as they did not understand the true dark nature of the Rakata who lived to conquer and destroy.<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> With the advent of the Rakatan [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], the species began to lose their influence on galactic politics.<ref name="TEA" />

In time, the Rakata came to desire the Infinity Gates of their former benefactors which was a secret the Kwa refused to share with them. This led to a war between the two races where the Kwa fought their former proteges on Lehon itself in order to destroy the Infinity Gate on the planet. Afterwards, the Kwa began to either destroy or disable the gates on other worlds whilst they retreated from Rakatan aggression. In time, the Kwa would retreat back to their homeworld of Dathomir though some remained on worlds such as [[Tython/Legends|Tython]].<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> After sealing the Infinity Gates and Star Temples, they set guardians to protect the Temples&mdash;giant [[whuffa worm]]s with thick hides and an impressive turn of speed.<ref name="ff" />

===Legacy===
Though the Infinite Empire wiped out the rest of the Kwa around the galaxy,<ref name="TEA" /> the original inhabitants of Dathomir eventually evolved&mdash;or rather degenerated&mdash;into the [[Kwi]].<ref name="ff" /> According to the beliefs of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], the usage of the Kwa Infinity Gates created unnatural voids and wounds to Dathomir that saw the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]] call the Infinite Empire to the planet. Their arrival decimated the Kwa who were transformed into an animal state by the action of the Spirits.<ref name="BoS:SftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Millennia later, many of the Kwa's descendants were slaughtered by the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] when the witches discovered the Gate.<ref name="Star Wars (1998) 24">[[Star Wars (1998) 24|''Star Wars'' (1998) 24]]</ref> The surviving Kwi fled into the desert where they would form tribes, including the [[Blue Desert People]]<ref name="CoPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> and the [[Blue Mountain People]].<ref name="YJK:SA">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref>
